sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages nete1240 (Nete) and biso1243 (Bisorio): reference lists and alternative names (Malamauda, Malaumanda, Iniai).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: 5 refs (Conrad & Lewis 1988, Davies & Comrie 1985, Dornstreich 1973, Franklin 2024, Ethnologue); zero grammar/phonology/sketch entries.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2026. Ethnologue: Languages of the World (online), entry Nete [net] -- free view.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Free view gives status 'stable', family, and 'Existing Content: NT (2015)'; population, dialects, language-development and typology fields are paywalled. Ethnologue typology lines rarely carry stress for PNG languages of this size; not a first-hand source in any case.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG Language & Culture Archives and SIL Global Language & Culture Archives: browse-by-language-code listings (letter N; letter B) and the SIL-PNG page 'Language: Nete [net]' (accessed 2026-09-20).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. Negative catalogue result: 'net' is absent from both the SIL-PNG list (37 N-codes) and the SIL Global list (231 N-codes), i.e. neither archive catalogues any item -- no Organised Phonology Data, no NTM phonemic statement, no Edmiston 1986 survey -- under Nete. This closes the the compilation's top works still to obtain (previously 'not accessible').

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Nete language' (accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.note: No phonology section; classification and village list only.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 2024. Engan fringe languages (North and South). Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 42: 94-110.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/tone. Comparative lexical paper (Nete vs Bisorio endings -se ~ -te, proto-Engan). p. 95: 'although Nete and Bisorio have been alluded to by Wurm and others, there has generally been a lack of data on these languages'; Nete data from SIL wordlists and Edmiston 1986 unpublished survey.

sources.citation: OLAC: Open Language Archives Community. 'OLAC resources in and about the Nete language' (ISO 639-3 net), combined catalog of all OLAC participants, up-to-date as of 2024-12-11 (the Internet Archive copy).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing; negative catalogue result A could not obtain (OLAC host down): only 4 items -- Rosetta Nete Swadesh List, Glottolog resources, Ethnologue entry, LINGUIST List page. No archive deposit (PARADISEC, TLA, Kaipuleohone, SIL L&CA, ANLA, AILLA..) exists for Nete in any OLAC-harvested archive.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. Newguineaworld: 'Nete' and 'Bisorio' pages (Trans-Enga > Nete-Bisorio), last modified 2024-06-25. newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch
sources.note: Phonology section reads in full: 'There is no published phonology of Nete.' (same for Bisorio). Gives Nete pronouns from Davies & Comrie's Iniai list in phonetic form with one stress mark (3dl niɛ-'mbʌ).

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (comp.). Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: 'Bisorio, Papua New Guinea'. Data supplied by Bob Kennell through Jason Stuart, Ethnos360 (NTM) Papua New Guinea, 31 October 2023. Leipzig: MPI-EVA (lingweb).
sources.note: No phonology content: body-part tally numerals 1-27 and stick counting to 90 in practical orthography, no stress or tone marks, no remarks on sounds.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Classification list only (best source = Davies & Comrie 1985 wordlist); the prosody overview concerns TNG generally and names no Engan-fringe language.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project (Long Now Foundation). n.d. [uploaded 2010-09-16]. Nete Swadesh List. Internet Archive item rosettaproject_net_swadesh-1 (84 entries).
sources.note: Nothing: bare gloss:form list in IPA-like transcription with the original phonetic stress marks removed; no notes.

sources.citation: SIL Papua New Guinea. 'PNG Language Resources: Language: Nete [net]' and 'PNG Bibliography.. by language' index (letters N and B), www-01.sil.org/pacific/png/, site copyright 2007-2013; the Internet Archive captures of 2015.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing; closes A's 'recorded for a later reading' item. The old SIL-PNG site, whose bibliography covered SIL's unpublished PNG manuscripts as well as publications, had no entry at all for Nete or Bisorio.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Australian National University. (Index of languages)
sources.note: Index cites only Wurm & Hattori 1981; nothing descriptive.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & Ron Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26, 243-273. Pacific Linguistics A-76.
sources.note: Nothing on Nete; survey wordlists (Pikaru/Bikaru argued to be a Bisorio dialect, pp. 249-250). No prosody statement.

sources.citation: Davies, John & Bernard Comrie. 1985. A linguistic survey of the Upper Yuat. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 22, 275-312. Pacific Linguistics A-63. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical survey; Nete mentioned only in passing (pp. 277, 282: 'Bisorio may be the same language as Nete'). Appendix reproduces Wayne Dye's Bisorio and Iniai wordlists with phonetic stress marks (e.g. Iniai niɛ-'mbʌ) but no statement of a stress rule.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. p. 51 entry 197 Bisorio: 'shows close relationships with the language called Nere (Nete, Neta) to the south.. probably a dialect of Maramuni Enga'. Checklist only.
